thread:
jordan: Following the RFC follow-up meeting, I want to capture a compact proposal for the "admission lifelines" surface. Goal: keep runtime9s call site tiny but provide enough signal for scheduler to avoid cold-warmup spikes.

maria: Short and concrete please. We need to ship a shim for Dedicated customers too.

ashwin: Proposal sketch: three runtime->scheduler calls: `probe_load(tenant, tokens_est, priority_hint)`, `ask_credits(tenant, tokens, soft_deadline_ms)`, `read_snapshot(tenant_list)`. Keep `probe_load` fire-and-forget (no backpressure).

devon: Implementation constraints: `read_snapshot` must be read-only and cheap. Make it eventual-consistent (TTL ~200ms) and return (queued_tokens, headroom, active_batches). No control semantics.

tiffany: Where does KV cache warmup live? If scheduler defers grants, warmup still needs to progress or we'll get long tails.

jordan: Introduce a tiny orthogonal token: `warmup_token`. Runtime can request at most N warmup_tokens per tenant per minute (configurable). Scheduler can `ACCEPT_WARMUP` or `REJECT`. ACCEPT lets the warmup path allocate a small fast-path slot that doesn't count against batch grants.

ashwin: Nice throttle. Add `warmup_effective_size` in response so runtime can estimate impact. Also return `warmup_quota_remaining`.

maria: We need metrics: warmup_token_requests, warmup_token_accepts, warmup_latency_ms, deferred_request_count, snapshot_age_ms. Add alerts for consecutive rejects > 5 for any tenant.

devon: For Dedicated compatibility, build a translator: legacy `lease_request` -> `ask_credits` with `soft_deadline_ms` mapped to lease TTL * 1000. Also translate lease `renew` into incremental `ask_credits` updates. Mark translator as a compatibility layer behind feature flag.

ops-bot: ci: queue-surface-e2e ran on branch admission-lifelines; 2 failing tests: `warmup_rate_limit` and `snapshot_staleness`.

tiffany: I'll take `warmup_rate_limit`. Quick thought: warmup_token should have two flavors: `SMALL` for <128 tokens that bypass, and `FULL` that wants a proper grant. Only SMALL gets fast-path. Keeps misuse low.

jordan: Good call. Add `token_type` in request. Runtime must annotate expected token_count. Scheduler can still reject if tenant hot.

ashwin: Proto draft for appendix (untested):
```
message ProbeLoad { string tenant = 1; int64 tokens_est = 2; int32 priority_hint = 3; }
message AskCredits { string tenant = 1; int64 tokens = 2; int64 soft_deadline_ms = 3; }
message WarmupRequest { string tenant = 1; int64 expected_tokens = 2; enum Type { SMALL = 0; FULL = 1; } type = 3; }
message CreditsReply { enum Outcome { GRANT = 0; DEFER = 1; REJECT = 2; } Outcome outcome = 1; int64 suggested_wait_ms = 2; int32 warmup_quota_remaining = 3; }
```

maria: Add a short test plan: unit tests for translator (lease->ask_credits), integration test where warmup SMALL bypasses but FULL waits, and flaky-sim test with snapshot TTL set to 50ms to ensure no tight spin. devon can sketch.

devon: Will add tests to the RFC follow-up. I'll also add a small synthetic load generator for the e2e to reproduce the `kv_warmup_under_defer` locally.

tiffany: If the rate-limit bypass helps, we should gate it behind `queue_warmup_bypass` FF and disable by default on Dedicated (to avoid expectations mismatch).

jordan: Agreed. Next steps: devon drops proto + tests, ashwin writes telemetry/alerts, tiffany runs warmup experiments. I'll author the RFC follow-up PR with rollback plan (remove translator & disable FF).

maria: Thanks. If we hit unexpected cold tails in staging, rollback = disable `queue_warmup_bypass` and enable `legacy_lease_translator=false`.

jordan: OK merging notes into the follow-up doc today. Ping here when you've pushed commits.
